text.p: Bonds were gaining in sympathy with other markets with investors optimistic that the latest U.S. inflation figures, due at 1230 GMT, will bring no bad news.
"I believe that the numbers (of the U.S. inflation) are going to be good and that our spreads in the coming weeks are going to reach historic lows," said one trader.
The 10-year spread with the cash Bund stood at 88 basis points, up from 81 on Monday, and compared with a record low of 80 basis points set in January.
But if the inflation figures were disappointing, the market could take some time to recover from the blow, the trader added.
But traders said that there was strong demand for the shorter dates, particularly on the OTC, and sooner or later this had to translate into higher prices.
"Spain cut the repo this morning, and a further cut by the Bank of Portugal is inevitable," said another trader.
